what: *** AND IT HOLDS 470 LERENA DOCUMENTS ***

Forty years and the wrong surname. ***

what: *** WHAT WAS VISIBLE IN THE FIRST HUNDRED, AND NOT FOLLOWED ***

what: *** THE 470 WAS THE BARRIO, NOT THE PARISH - CORRECTED THE SAME DAY ***
the query: the 470 hits paged to the end: 95 of the first 100 are Nuestra Senora del Carmen La Mayor volumes, and *** pages 2 and 3 contain NOT ONE ***
result: *** THE PARISH'S OWN SHARE IS ABOUT 95, NOT 470 ***
what was already known: This file said this morning that the Cordon parish holds 470 documents of this surname, called it the largest unworked seam in the archive, and warned that an errand understating its own size is how a seam stays unopened for a month.
what it means: *** IT THEN OVERSTATED ITS OWN SIZE BY FIVE TIMES. *** q.anyPlace=Cordon scopes the *** NEIGHBOURHOOD ***, and most of the 470 are other Montevideo parishes and civil registers whose people simply lived there - La Union, Pocitos, San Francisco de Asis, the Catedral, the Montevideo marriage registers. *** The parish hits are ranked first and are essentially exhausted on page one. *** Controlled properly this time: a fake sub-place, 'Nonesuch, Montevideo', returns 26 pages - the whole department - while Cordon returns 5, so the filter DOES resolve Cordon; what it resolves it to is the barrio.

what: *** AND THAT IS GOOD NEWS, WHICH IS THE ODD PART ***
the query: the same count, read for what it means for the work
result: *** 95 DOCUMENTS ACROSS 43 VOLUMES IS AN AFTERNOON, NOT A CAMPAIGN ***
what was already known: The errand was rewritten this morning to say the Cordon 'will not be done in an afternoon' and left open with 470 against it.
what it means: *** It can be done in an afternoon, and the errand now says so. *** The volumes with the most hits are *** Religious Marriage Records 1916-1926 (6) ***, *** the bundled Rite Registers / Marriage Dispensation / Religious Marriage Records 1895-1898 (5) ***, and four each in the baptism registers of *** 1869-1872, 1904-1908 and 1908-1910. *** The parish runs baptisms 1828-1923, marriages 1842-1931, burials and deaths 1839-1926, and this archive's surname appears across the whole span.

what: *** A SECOND DISPENSATION BOOK, AT PARISH LEVEL ***
the query: Nuestra Senora del Carmen La Mayor, bundled volume: *** Religious Rite Registers 1895-1898, MARRIAGE DISPENSATION RECORDS 1895-1898, Religious Marriage Records 1895-1898 *** - five Lerena hits
result: *** THE ARQUIDIOCESIS REGISTER IS NOT THE ONLY ONE ***
what was already known: This morning's sweep concluded there is no tenth Lerena dispensation, on the Arquidiocesis de Montevideo register of 1856-1932, searched on eight compound forms to the end of every result set.
what it means: *** That conclusion is about that book and it stands - but a PARISH kept dispensation records of its own, and this one has five hits. *** Two were opened at the transcript. *** Both turn out to be CIVIL MARRIAGE TESTIMONIOS copied into the parish book rather than dispensations *** - the volume bundles three record types under one title. So it is not yet a tenth dispensation; it is a book nobody here knew existed, and three of its five hits are unread.

what: *** AND THE CARVALLO LERENA LEAD IS PARTLY WORKED ***

Carvallo Lerena'. *** A second hit, ark 5SX5-3, gives a *** Don Arturo Rivas Lerena, born 13 August 1872 in this city, son of Maximo Rivas (deceased) and Armela Luna *** - but his parents carry no Lerena between them, so the compound may be the machine's. *** The transcript writes Montevideo as 'Monterdes', so nothing here is tiered and both need the plate. ***

what: *** AND THE CORDON SWEEP ANSWERED A QUESTION THIS REGISTER ASKED YESTERDAY ***
the query: the Manuel Antonio Lerena of the Cordon snippet, traced through the record index - ark FL9R-R9Z, VR4D-NMH
result: *** HE IS THE SON OF PEDRO A. LERENA AND MANUELA LEMOS, born 31 March 1883, christened at Montevideo on 9 April ***
what was already known: On 11 October this archive entered *** MANUELA LEMOS (m. Pedro A. LERENA) *** with two children fifteen years apart - Felicia Clementina (b. c.1868, m. 1886) and Manuel Antonio (b. 1883) - and wrote on her row, in terms: *** WHICH PEDRO LERENA SHE MARRIED IS NOT SETTLED. ***
what it means: *** THE 1896 DEATH RECORD FOUND TODAY NAMES HER HUSBAND'S PARENTS. *** 'Pedro a Lerena', died 6 November 1896 aged *** 69 ***, certificate 353, Montevideo - *** spouse MANUELA LEMOS ***, father *** Pedro A. Lerena ***, mother *** VICENTA DE LA VEGA. *** So the Pedro she married is a son of Pedro Antonio Lerena and Vicenta Vega - which is the parentage of *** PEDRO LERENA VEGA ***, counted at sixteen in Montevideo household 229 about 1833. *** Two questions asked from opposite ends meet on one record. ***

what: *** AND THE AGE PROBLEM GETS BETTER, NOT WORSE ***
the query: the two estimates compared
result: *** 1817 FROM A CENSUS AGE, 1827 FROM AN AGE AT DEATH - AND 1827 FITS THE CHILDREN ***
what was already known: The register has carried Pedro LERENA Vega as born about 1817, from being entered at sixteen in the household-229 census, and today's row noted the decade's disagreement as a reason not to merge.
what it means: *** A man born in 1827 fathers a child in 1883 at fifty-six; a man born in 1817 does it at sixty-six. *** Neither is impossible and the first is ordinary. *** So the death record's age is the likelier of the two, and the census age is the one to doubt *** - which is the opposite of how this archive weighted them this afternoon. *** STILL NOT MERGED. *** Both sides are index-level: the 1896 death act has not been opened, and neither has the household-229 image been re-read for his age. *** That is now the single cheapest thing that would attach a whole Montevideo line to this archive's trunk. ***

what: *** AND THE PARAGUAYAN IS PROBABLY NOT PARAGUAYAN ***
the query: the Cordon snippet 'D. Manuel Antonio Lerena araguayo soltero', against the index
result: *** HE IS BORN AT MONTEVIDEO ***
what was already known: The last of the four Cordon leads was a Manuel Antonio Lerena recorded *** paraguayo ***, a nationality this archive has never met.
what it means: *** The only Manuel Antonio Lerena the index places in Montevideo is born there on 31 March 1883 *** to Pedro A. Lerena and Manuela Lemos, and married Esther EVIA, with sons *** Manuel Walter Lerena (b. 16 November 1921) *** and Alberto Nestor Lerena Evia. *** So either the Cordon record is a different man, or 'araguayo' is the machine's reading of something else *** - the same transcript writes Montevideo as 'Monterdes'. *** The lead is not closed and the plate has not been opened ***, but a Paraguayan branch should not be written down on this evidence. *** For the record: the whole index holds ONE Lerena record in Paraguay. ***

what: *** THE ACT WAS OPENED THE SAME EVENING, AND IT CONFIRMS THE INDEX ***
the query: Montevideo, Death Records 1896, *** acta No. 353 of 7 November 1896 *** - image ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS2W-H39V-V, plate read at apid TH-909-72188-82458-0
result: *** PEDRO LERENA, BORN AT MONTEVIDEO, DIED 6 NOVEMBER 1896 AGED SIXTY-NINE ***
what was already known: This was raised as an errand an hour earlier and called the cheapest act in the archive, on the strength of an index entry.
what it means: *** Before Vicente Carricaonde, Juez de Paz of the 15th section of the Capital. *** Died at five in the afternoon of the previous day at *** calle Rivera No. 163 ***, of *** tisis pulmonar ***, certified by *** Dr Vitale. *** Oriental, *** nacido en Montevideo ***, casado. *** HIJO LEGITIMO DE DON PEDRO A. LERENA, ORIENTAL, FALLECIDO, Y DE DONA VICENTA DE LA VEGA, ORIENTAL, FALLECIDA. *** The index is confirmed at the plate.

what: *** AND THE WIFE AND CHILDREN ARE NAMED IN THE CLOSING PARAGRAPH ***
the query: the same act
result: *** MANUELA, 53, AND THE CHILDREN ANTONIO, CARLOS TEODORO AND MANUEL ANTONIO ***
what was already known: The register has held MANUELA LEMOS since 11 October with two children - Felicia Clementina (b. c.1868) and Manuel Antonio (b. 1883) - and an explicit note that which Pedro she married was not settled.
what it means: *** 'el finado era casado con Dona Manuela, Oriental, de 53 anos, y de cuyo matrimonio existen ... Antonio = Carlos Teodoro = Manuel Antonio ... y que el primer declarante es hijo del fallecido.' *** So the household gains *** ANTONIO and CARLOS TEODORO ***, and the first declarant - *** Don Pedro A. Lerena, soltero, empleado *** - is named as the dead man's son. *** The second declarant is Angel V. Garcia, 25, soltero, empleado. *** Manuela at 53 was born about 1843.

what: *** WHAT IT SETTLES, AND WHAT IT BREAKS ***
the query: the act against the c.1833 census of household 229
result: *** SETTLED: which Pedro married Manuela Lemos. BROKEN: the date of household 229. ***
what was already known: Pedro LERENA Vega has been carried here as born about 1817, from being entered at sixteen in Montevideo household 229, which this archive dates c.1833.
what it means: *** The act is primary and specific: born at Montevideo, sixty-nine in November 1896, so born about 1827. *** A man born in 1827 is *** six *** in 1833, not sixteen - he is sixteen in *** 1843. *** So one of two things is true: the census is later than this archive dates it, or the sixteen-year-old is a different son of the same couple. *** The act names his parents outright, so the ATTACHMENT is not in doubt either way *** - he is a son of Pedro Antonio Lerena and Vicenta de la Vega. *** What is now in doubt is a date this archive has been using for a census, which is a better problem than the one it replaces. ***

what: *** THE ERRAND WAS ANSWERED AND THE ANSWER IS 'CONTESTED' ***
the query: Uruguay census, household 229 - image ark 3:1:3QS7-99ZP-BBKX, plate read at apid TH-1951-36718-25784-7
result: *** FAMILYSEARCH LABELS THE VOLUME 'Montevideo. Census 1850'. THIS ARCHIVE DATES THE HOUSEHOLD c.1833. BOTH CANNOT BE RIGHT. ***
what was already known: An errand was raised an hour earlier to re-date household 229, on the assumption that the c.1833 was a loose guess and the death act would overturn it.
what it means: *** IT IS NOT A LOOSE GUESS. *** The head is entered as *** 'D. Pedro A. Lerena, varon, 40' ***, and this archive holds a *** PEDRO ANTONIO LERENA BORN 31 JULY 1793 ***, son of Sancho, married to a *** VICENTA VEGA of Cerro Largo *** - the exact couple on the census line, attested independently by a Catedral baptism of 4 July 1837 and by both of them standing godparents at the Aguada on 21 November 1852. *** A man born in 1793 is forty in 1833. *** So the c.1833 was inferred from an attested birth, which is a better basis than a volume label - and the volume label says 1850, when he would have been fifty-seven.

what: *** WHAT THE HOUSEHOLD ACTUALLY SAYS ***
the query: the same plate, 2a Seccion, read line by line
result: *** FIVE PEOPLE, AND THE SURNAME CARRIED DOWN BY DITTO ***
what was already known: The register has carried three children from this household with birth years derived from their ages.
what it means: *** 229 - D. Pedro A. Lerena, varon, 40 | D.a Vicenta Vega, muger, 35 | D.a Emilia Lerena, 18 | D.n Pedro D.o [dicho], varon, 16 | D.a Vicenta D.o, muger, [age struck]. *** The sons and daughters carry the surname only as *** D.o *** - dicho, ditto - which is worth noting in an archive whose whole problem is how this name gets written down.

what: *** AND THE THREE DATINGS DO NOT AGREE ***
the query: the census age against the death act read earlier this evening
result: *** 1817, 1827 OR 1834 - THREE ANCHORS, THREE ANSWERS ***
what was already known: Pedro the son is sixteen on the census; the death act of 7 November 1896 makes him sixty-nine.
what it means: *** If the census is 1833 he was born about 1817 and would be SEVENTY-NINE in 1896. If it is 1850 he was born about 1834 and would be SIXTY-TWO. The act says SIXTY-NINE, which wants a census of about 1843. *** No two of the three agree. *** THE ATTACHMENT IS NOT AFFECTED - the death act names his parents outright - but THREE BIRTH YEARS IN THIS REGISTER REST ON A CENSUS DATE THAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED: *** Emilia LERENA Vega, Pedro LERENA Vega and Vicenta LERENA Vega, all three carried as c.1815, c.1817 and c.1821. *** They are now marked as resting on it. ***

what: *** WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT ***
the query: the census volume itself
result: *** THE ENUMERATION'S OWN DATE, WHICH THIS PAGE DOES NOT CARRY ***
what was already known: The page gives '2a Seccion', a street and a house number, and no year.
what it means: *** Either a title page or a certifying signature elsewhere in the volume, or the FamilySearch catalogue entry for the item behind image group M9Z3-PQJ. *** Until one of those is read, the honest position is that *** household 229 is undated *** and its three derived birth years are estimates resting on an assumption, not on a record. *** That is a worse position than this archive thought it was in an hour ago, and it is the true one. ***

what: *** AND THE 1850 IS ITEM-LEVEL, WHICH MAKES IT STRONGER THAN A VOLUME LABEL ***
the query: the viewer's own breadcrumb: *** 'Montevideo. Census 1850 - #007499042 > Item 2' ***, film 007499042 ('Uruguay, Canelones, censos', 3,290 images)
result: *** THE DATE IS ATTACHED TO THE ITEM, NOT TO THE FILM ***
what was already known: This archive has a standing rule, learned the hard way, that a FILM's label can describe only its first segment and must never be trusted for frames deeper in - the waypoint lesson.
what it means: *** THAT RULE DOES NOT RESCUE THE c.1833 HERE. *** The 1850 is not the film's label; the film is a general 'censos' reel and *** the 1850 is item 2's own title ***, which is the level the rule says to trust. *** So the evidence now tilts to 1850 *** - and the cost of accepting it is large: the head at forty would be born about 1810, which is *** NOT Pedro Antonio Lerena, son of Sancho, born 31 July 1793. ***

what: *** WHAT ACCEPTING 1850 WOULD COST ***
the query: the consequence, written down before anyone acts on it
result: *** IT WOULD DETACH HOUSEHOLD 229 FROM SANCHO'S LINE ***
what was already known: The household is currently read as Sancho's son Pedro Antonio with his wife Vicenta Vega and their children, and three birth years are derived from it.
what it means: *** If the enumeration is 1850 then its head, aged forty, was born about 1810 and is a DIFFERENT Pedro A. Lerena *** - and this register already warns that more than one exists, naming a separate Pedro Antonio Lerena who married Teresa Leonard. The children's years would move to about 1832, 1834 and 1838, and the household would no longer be evidence of Sancho's son at all. *** THAT IS TOO MUCH TO CHANGE ON A BREADCRUMB. *** What settles it is the enumeration's own date inside the volume, or the catalogue entry for item 2 of film 007499042. *** Until then household 229 stays as it is, flagged, with the conflict published rather than resolved by preference. ***

what: *** SETTLED AT CATALOGUE LEVEL: THE PADRON OF 1850 ***
the query: FamilySearch catalogue *** koha:1408224, 'Uruguay, Montevideo, censos, 1726-1860' *** - film 7499042 listed item by item
what was already known: An hour ago this file said the date was contested and that the breadcrumb alone was too little to act on.
what it means: *** The household sits in ITEM 2, so the enumeration is the PADRON OF 1850 - libro 264 - and the catalogue names the actual register book, which no label had. *** Two independent sources now agree: the viewer's breadcrumb and the catalogue entry. *** c.1833 IS WITHDRAWN. ***

what: *** AND THE IDENTIFICATION DOES NOT SURVIVE IT ***
the query: the head's age against an attested birth
result: *** THE HEAD OF HOUSEHOLD 229 IS NOT SANCHO'S SON ***
what was already known: The household has been read as Pedro Antonio Lerena, born 31 July 1793, with his wife Vicenta Vega - and the c.1833 dating was itself inferred from that reading.
what it means: *** The error was circular: the date was chosen to fit the identification, and the identification then rested on the date. *** Entered at *** forty *** in 1850, the head was born about *** 1810. *** And the correction holds even under the neighbouring book: in the 1843 padron he would be born about 1803, still not 1793. *** So under EITHER candidate volume he is too young ***, and household 229 stops being evidence of Sancho's son. *** What it still is: a Pedro A. Lerena married to a Vicenta Vega, with three children - which is the same couple the Catedral baptism of 4 July 1837 attests, so either that couple is not Sancho's son's either, or one of the two records is badly wrong about an age. *** Published unresolved rather than argued either way.

what: *** THREE BIRTH YEARS MOVED SEVENTEEN YEARS ***
the query: the three children of household 229
result: *** Emilia c.1815 to c.1832 | Pedro c.1817 to c.1834 | Vicenta c.1821 to c.1838 ***
what was already known: All three were derived from ages on a census this archive dated c.1833.
what it means: *** The ages on the plate are unchanged - 18, 16 and an age struck through - so only the subtraction changed. *** The rows, the relations file and the person-pairs declarations were all moved together, which is the part that usually gets missed. *** One residue: the 1896 death act makes Pedro sixty-nine, implying about 1827, where the 1850 padron implies 1834. Seven years, on an age given by a son at a desk. Recorded, not reconciled. ***
